For the distance between the heaven and the earth is not covered on foot except in years, so wings were given to them so that they might reach the distant place in a short time, like birds.

﴿He increases in creation what He wills﴾: this confirms what arises in souls of wonder and astonishment at the report of the angels possessing wings; that is, this is no novelty in God's power, for He increases in His creation what He wills. The apparent meaning is the generality of creation. al-Farrāʾ said: this refers to the wings that the angels have, that is, He increases the wings in the creation of the angels. They also said: this increase includes beautiful form, or beautiful voice, or beautiful handwriting, or elegance in the eyes or nose, or lightness of spirit, or beauty, or curly hair, or intellect, or knowledge, or craftsmanship, or chastity among the poor, or sweetness in the mouth; these sayings are given by way of example, not restriction. The verse is absolute and encompasses every increase in creation, and they have explained this increase by desirable things; and "what He wills" is general and does not specify one desirable thing over another. He concluded the verse with ﴿power over everything﴾, which indicates this. Opening and sending are a metaphor for releasing, and ﴿none can send it forth﴾ stands in place of ﴿none can open it﴾; the meaning is: whatever God seeks.

﴿of mercy﴾: that is, of blessing and provision, or rain, or health, or security, or other kinds of His favors that cannot be counted. What is reported from the early exegetes about explaining mercy by a particular thing is not meant as a restriction; it is only an example. al-Zamakhsharī said: the indefiniteness of "mercy" is for generality and vagueness, as if he said: of whatever mercy it may be, heavenly or earthly, no one can hold it back or restrain it, and whatever God withholds, no one can release it. End of quote. The generality is understood from the conditional noun and from "of mercy" serving to clarify that general term as to what kind it is. This is one of the cases where the indefinite singular is used in place of the definite plural which corresponds in generality to the conditional noun; its implied form is: of mercies. "Min" is in the position of a circumstantial clause, i.e., being among mercies, and it cannot be in the position of an attribute because the conditional noun is not qualified. The apparent meaning is that His saying ﴿and whatever He withholds﴾ is general, covering mercy and other things, since no specification was mentioned for it; so it remains general over everything He withholds. If its explanation is ﴿of mercy﴾ and it has been omitted because the first indicates it, then the masculine pronoun in ﴿none can send it forth after Him﴾ is taken according to the wording of "mā," while the feminine in ﴿none can withhold it﴾ is taken according to its meaning, since its meaning is mercy. It was also read: "fa-lā mursila lahā," with the feminine pronoun, and this is evidence that the explanation is ﴿of mercy﴾, which was omitted because the preceding clause indicates it. From Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿of mercy﴾ is of the category of repentance (tawbah), ﴿none can withhold it﴾, i.e., they repent if they wish and if they refuse; ﴿and whatever He withholds﴾ is of the category of ..., ﴿none can send it forth after Him﴾, so they do not repent. Also from him: ﴿of mercy﴾ means of guidance. al-Zamakhsharī said: If you say: what do you say about one who explained mercy as repentance and attributed it to Ibn ʿAbbās? I say: he meant by repentance: guidance toward it and success in it, which is what Ibn ʿAbbās meant; if he said it, it is acceptable; but if he meant that if the sinner wills to repent he repents, and if he does not will, he does not repent, it is rejected, because God wills repentance forever, and it is not permissible for Him not to will it. End of quote, and this is in the way of the Muʿtazilah.

﴿after Him﴾ is by omission of a noun: that is, after His withholding, like His saying ﴿who then can guide him after God?﴾ [al-Jāthiyah: 23], i.e., after God's leading astray of him, because before it is ﴿and God led him astray knowingly﴾, like His saying ﴿whom God leads astray, there is no guide for him﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 186]. al-Zamakhsharī estimated it as "after the guidance of God," which is a faulty estimate that does not suit the verse; he proceeded in it in the way of the Muʿtazilah.

﴿And He is the Mighty﴾: the Overpowering, capable of sending and withholding; ﴿the Wise﴾: who sends and withholds according to what His wisdom requires.

﴿O people﴾: address to the Quraysh, and it is directed to every believer and disbeliever, especially whoever worships other than God; and He reminded them of His blessings in their creation. ﴿Remember﴾ is not a command to remember with the tongue, but with it and with the heart, and by guarding the blessing from ingratitude and by thanking; like your saying to one whom you have favored: "Remember my favors upon you," meaning preserve them and be thankful for them. All are immersed in God's blessing. So the address is general in wording, even though this was revealed because of the Quraysh; then He asked as a question for the purpose of affirmation.

﴿Is there any creator other than God?﴾ That is: there is no god except the Creator; what you worship of idols is not. Ibn Wththāb, Shaqīq, Abū Jaʿfar, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ﴿ghayri﴾ in the genitive, as an adjective agreeing with the wording, and ﴿min khāliq﴾ is the subject. ﴿Provides for you﴾: they permitted it to be the predicate of the subject, or an attribute of it, or a new sentence, and on these two possibilities the predicate is omitted, its estimate being "for you." Shaybah, ʿĪsā, al-Ḥasan and the rest of the seven read ﴿ghayru﴾ in the nominative, and they permitted it to be an adjective agreeing with the position, just as the predicate was an adjective agreeing with the wording; and this is more apparent for the harmony of the two readings; and that it be the predicate of the subject, and that it be the agent of the active participle ﴿khāliq﴾, since it relies on the interrogative particle, so its governing is permitted, like your saying: "Is Zayd standing?" according to one of its aspects. In this there is consideration: that an active participle, or what functions like it, when it relies on an interrogative particle and is made to function like a verb so that it raises what follows it, can one prefix to it "min" of universal quantification, saying "Is there any standing man, the Zaydūn?" as you say "Is standing the Zaydūn?" The apparent view is that it is not permitted. Do you not see that when it functions like a verb, it does not contain generality, contrary to when you prefix "min" to it? I do not know a parallel to it in the speech of the Arabs, and one should not advance the permissibility of such a thing except with a hearing from Arabic speech. Al-Faḍl ibn Ibrāhīm al-Naḥwī read ﴿ghayra﴾ in the accusative as an exception, and the predicate is either ﴿provides for you﴾ or an omitted one, and ﴿provides for you﴾ is a new sentence; and when ﴿provides for you﴾ is a new sentence it is better, because the truth of "creator" applied to other than God is negated, unlike when it is an attribute, for an attribute restricts, so there would be a creator other than God, but he would not be a provider. The meaning of ﴿from the heaven﴾ is with rain, ﴿and the earth﴾ with plants; ﴿there is no god but Him﴾ is an independent sentence with no place in the grammatical structure.

﴿Then how are you turned away?﴾: that is, how are they turned from monotheism to polytheism; and "that they deny you" leads to matters; the discussion of this has already been given.

﴿Indeed the promise of God is true﴾: it encompasses all that He promised of reward, punishment and other things. The majority read ﴿al-gharūr﴾ with a fatḥah on the ghayn, and Ibn ʿAbbās explained it as the Shayṭān. Abū Ḥaywah and Abū al-Sammāl read it with a ḍammah, as the plural of gharr, or as a verbal noun, like His saying ﴿and he made them fall by deception﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 22]. The discussion of this has already been covered at the end of Luqmān.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 35, verses 1–8 (part 3 of 3):

﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you.﴾ His enmity dates back to our father Adam. And what greater enmity is there than that he said about his descendants, ﴿I will surely mislead them all﴾ [Sad: 82], ﴿and I will surely lead them astray﴾ [an-Nisa: 119]? ﴿So take him as an enemy﴾, meaning by boycotting and opposing him, by following the Sharia. Then he explained that his aim in calling his party was only to have them tormented in the Fire, sharing the punishment with them. He is therefore extremely eager for this, so that he may prove the truth of his words, ﴿I will surely mislead them﴾ [al-Hijr: 39], ﴿and I will surely lead them astray﴾ [an-Nisa: 119]. For sharing in what is harmful may bring some consolation, unlike being alone in punishment. Then he mentioned the two groups and what has been prepared for each of them of punishment and reward. He began with the disbelievers because of the proximity to his words, ﴿He only calls his party﴾, so he followed the report about the disbeliever with his state in the Hereafter. Ibn Atiyyah said: The lam in ﴿liyakūna﴾ ("that they may be") is the lam of becoming (lam al-sayrurah), because he did not call them to the blaze; rather, it happened that their affair became, as a result of his calling, to that end. End of quotation. We say: This is of what is expressed by the cause, using what results from it: their being called to disbelief, and the punishment resulting from it. And ﴿those who disbelieved﴾ and ﴿those who believed﴾ are subjects (mubtada'an). Some allowed that ﴿those who disbelieved﴾ could be in the genitive position as a substitute (badal) for ﴿the companions of the blaze﴾, or as a descriptive qualifier (sifah), and in the accusative position as a substitute for ﴿his party﴾, and in the nominative position as a substitute for the pronoun in ﴿liyakūnū﴾. All of this is far from the eloquence of the division and the strength of the structure.

﴿Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him, so that he sees it as good [...]﴾: meaning, so that he sees the evil of his deed as good. Man (من) is a relative subject (mubtada' mawsul), and its predicate is omitted. What the analysis requires is that the implied meaning be: "like one for whom it has not been made attractive," as in His words, ﴿Is one who is upon clear evidence from his Lord like one for whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive?﴾ [Muhammad: 14], ﴿Is one who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind?﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 19], ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life...?﴾ [al-An'am: 122], then He said, ﴿like one whose likeness is in darkness﴾ [al-An'am: 122]. This was said by al-Kisa'i, meaning its implied form is: "his soul goes out after them in regrets," because of the indication of ﴿so do not let your soul go out after them﴾. It was also said that the implied meaning is: "he saw it as good, so Allah misguided him, like one whom Allah guided," so that was omitted because of the indication of ﴿Indeed, Allah misguides whom He wills﴾. Az-Zajjaj mentioned these two views. Az-Zamakhshari explained here ﴿He misguides whom He wills﴾ according to his method in various places of his book, that misguidance is His forsaking him and leaving him to his own affair, and he used many expressions to this meaning. The majority read ﴿Is one whose [evil deed] has been made attractive﴾ in the passive voice, with ﴿evil﴾ in the nominative case (sū'u). ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read: zayyana la-hu sū'a, in the active voice, with sū'a in the accusative. He is also reported to have read asū'a in the form of af'al in the accusative. The worst of his deed is shirk. The reading of Talhah is: a-man without the fa'. The author of al-Lawami said: It is an interrogative with the meaning of the common reading, for affirmation (taqrir). It may also be in the meaning of the vocative particle, so the complete form has been omitted, as the answer has been omitted in the well-known form. End of quotation. By "the answer" he means the predicate of the subject, and by "the complete form" he means what is conveyed by it, meaning: reflect and return to Allah. ﴿Indeed, Allah misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾ is a consolation to the Messenger (ﷺ) regarding the disbelief of his people, and an obligation of submission to Allah in His misguiding whom He wills and guiding whom He wills. The majority read ﴿So do not let your soul go [after them]﴾ in the active voice from dhahaba, with nafsuka as the subject. Abu Ja'far, Qatadah, ʿIsa, al-Ashhab, Shaybah, Abu Haywah, Humayd, al-A'mash, and Ibn Muhaysin read tudhhib from adhhaba, with the pronoun of the addressee ﴿your soul﴾ as the object in the accusative. It is narrated from Nafi'. Al-hasrah is the grief of the soul over the loss of a matter. ﴿Regrets﴾ (hasarat) is in the accusative as a object of purpose (maf'ul min ajlihi), meaning: "do not let your soul perish out of regrets." ʿAlayhim is related to ﴿tadhhab﴾, as you say: "he perished for him out of love," and "he died for him out of sorrow." Or it is an explanation of the one regretted over, and it is not related to ḥasarāt because it is a verbal noun, and its complement cannot precede it. Az-Zamakhshari said: It may also be a circumstantial state (hal), as if all of it became regrets due to the intensity of grief, as Jarir said:

*Ceaseless heat has worn their flesh away along with the night-journey, until they departed as breasts and chests.*

He means: they returned as breasts and chests, that is, nothing remained except their breasts and chests. From the same is His saying:

*Upon their trail my soul falls away in regrets, and their remembrance for me is sickness.*

End of quotation. What was mentioned, that "breasts and chests" are circumstantial states, is the view of Sibawayh. Al-Mubarrad said: It is a specification (tamyiz) transferred from the subject, meaning: until their breasts and chests departed. Then He threatened them with punishment for their evil conduct, saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾, meaning: He will therefore recompense them for it.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 35, verses 1–8 (part 1 of 3):

Surat Fatir is Meccan, and it has forty-five verses.
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿All praise is due to Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, who made the angels messengers having wings, two or three or four. He adds to creation what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾ ﴿Whatever mercy Allah grants to people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release after Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ ﴿O mankind, remember the favor of Allah upon you. Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? There is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded?﴾ ﴿And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then already were messengers denied before you. And to Allah are returned all matters.﴾ ﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is true, so let not the worldly life delude you, and let not the Deceiver delude you concerning Allah.﴾ ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party that they may be among the companions of the Blaze.﴾ ﴿Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment, but those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ ﴿Then is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him so that he sees it as good [equal to one guided]? For indeed, Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So do not let yourself go in grief over them. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.﴾ ﴿And it is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, and We drive them to a dead land and revive thereby the earth after its death. Thus will be the resurrection.﴾ [Fatir: 9] ﴿Whoever desires honor — to Allah belongs all honor. To Him ascends good speech, and righteous deeds raise it. But those who plot evil deeds will have a severe punishment, and the plotting of those — it will perish.﴾ [Fatir: 10] ﴿And Allah created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then made you into pairs. No female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge. And no one is granted a lengthened life or has his life shortened except that it is in a Record. Indeed, that is easy for Allah.﴾ [Fatir: 11] ﴿And not alike are the two bodies of water: one is sweet, fresh, pleasant to drink, and the other is salty and bitter. And from both you eat fresh meat and extract ornaments you wear, and you see the ships plowing through them that you may seek of His bounty; and perhaps you will be grateful.﴾ [Fatir: 12] ﴿He merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running to a specified term. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. And those you invoke other than Him do not possess [so much as] a date-pit membrane.﴾ [Fatir: 13] ﴿If you invoke them, they do not hear your call; and if they heard, they would not respond to you. And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your associating them with Him. And none can inform you like an [All-]Acquainted.﴾ [Fatir: 14] ﴿O mankind, you are the poor toward Allah, and Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.﴾ [Fatir: 15] ﴿If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation.﴾ [Fatir: 16] ﴿And that is not difficult for Allah.﴾ [Fatir: 17] ﴿No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a relative. You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen and establish prayer. And whoever purifies himself does so only for his own soul. And to Allah is the destination.﴾ [Fatir: 18] ﴿And not alike are the blind and the seeing,﴾ [Fatir: 19] ﴿nor are darknesses and light,﴾ [Fatir: 20] ﴿nor shade and heat,﴾ [Fatir: 21] ﴿nor are the living and the dead alike. Indeed, Allah causes to hear whom He wills, but you cannot make hear those who are in the graves.﴾ [Fatir: 22] ﴿You are not but a warner.﴾ [Fatir: 23] ﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them.﴾ [Fatir: 24] ﴿And if they deny you, those before them had already denied; their messengers came to them with clear proofs and with scriptures and with the illuminating Book.﴾ [Fatir: 25] ﴿Then I seized those who disbelieved, so how was My denunciation!﴾ [Fatir: 26] ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down rain from the sky, and We bring forth thereby fruits of varying colors? And among the mountains are white and red streaks of varying shades, and [others] extremely black.﴾ [Fatir: 27] ﴿And among people and moving creatures and livestock are those of various colors. Thus, among His servants, only the knowledgeable fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might, Forgiving.﴾ [Fatir: 28] ﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah, establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, hope for a commerce that will never perish,﴾ [Fatir: 29] ﴿that He may give them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty. Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾ [Fatir: 30] ﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth, confirming what was before it. Indeed, Allah is, concerning His servants, All-Knowing and Seeing.﴾ [Fatir: 31] ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants; then among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah. That is the great bounty.﴾ [Fatir: 32] ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence they will enter, adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their clothing therein is silk.﴾ [Fatir: 33] ﴿And they will say, "All praise is due to Allah, who has removed from us grief. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative,﴾ [Fatir: 34] ﴿who has settled us in the home of settlement from His bounty; there touches us not fatigue, nor touches us therein weariness."﴾ [Fatir: 35]

Al-Qitmir: it is well known that it is the thin skin that is on the date-pit, and the statements of the exegetes will come. Al-judad: plural of judda, which is a path formed in the land or the mountain, like a great piece continuous in length. Al-Zamakhshari said: al-judad are the streaks and the paths. Labid said: "or a course (judad) of the single one." It is said: judda of the donkey for the black mark on its back, and a gazelle may have two musk-scented streaks separating the colors of its back and its belly. End. The poet said:

"As if the streaks and the judda of its back were beads among which glitters a gleam."

The judda: the line that is in the middle of its back, describing a wild donkey. Al-gharibib: the intensely black. Laghiba yalghabu lughuban: he became weary.

* *

This surah is Meccan. When Allah, exalted, mentioned at the end of the preceding surah the destruction of the disbelievers, enemies of the believers, and placed them in the abodes of punishment, it became incumbent upon the believers to praise Him, to thank Him for His blessings, and to describe Him with His great favors, as in His saying: ﴿So the last of the people who did wrong were cut off. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-An'am: 45].

Al-Dahhak and al-Zuhri read fatara, making it a past-tense verb and putting in the accusative what follows it. Abu al-Fadl al-Razi said: either by supposing an implied alladhi, so that it is an epithet for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; or by estimating qad before it, so that it has the sense of a circumstantial clause. End. Omitting the relative noun is not permitted according to the Basrans. As for the circumstantial clause, it would be a narrated circumstance; but the better view, in my opinion, is that it is the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e., He is the One who originated (fatara). The explanation of ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾ has already been given, and that the meaning is "creator of them after they were not." The heavens and the earth are an expression for the world.

Abu Abdullah al-Razi said: praise is generally for a blessing, and Allah's blessings are immediate. ﴿Praise be to Allah who created the heavens and the earth and made darknesses and light﴾ [al-An'am: 1] points to the immediate blessing, and its evidence is ﴿He is the One who created you from clay, then decreed a term﴾ [al-An'am: 2]. And ﴿Praise be to Allah who revealed to His servant the Book﴾ [al-Kahf: 1] also points to it; and it is piety, for piety and righteousness come through the Law and the Book. Praise in Surat Saba' points to the blessing of bringing into being and of gathering, and its evidence is ﴿He knows what enters the earth and what emerges from it﴾ [Saba': 2], and His saying ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us"﴾ [Saba': 3]. And here it points to the blessing of endurance in the Hereafter, and its evidence is ﴿and the angels will receive them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 103]. (So Fatir of the heavens and the earth is the one who splits them, for the descent of spirits from the sky and the emergence of bodies from the earth; its evidence is ﴿Who made the angels messengers having wings﴾, that is, on that day.) Thus the beginning of this surah is connected to the end of what came before; because "as was done with their likes before" is a clarification of the cutting off of the hope of one who was in disquieting doubt. When He mentioned their state, He mentioned the state of the believer and gave him good news of the sending of the angels to them as bringers of good tidings, and that He opens for them the doors of mercy.

al-Hasan read jaʿiluh with nominative (jāʿilun), i.e., He is the maker; ʿAbd al-Warith from Abu ʿAmr read jaʿilu with nominative without tanwin, and al-malāʾikata in the accusative, the tanwin being dropped because of the meeting of two unvocalized letters. Ibn Yaʿmar and Khulayd ibn Nashit read jaʿala as a past-tense verb, with al-malāʾikata in the accusative, after reading fāṭiri with an alif and the genitive, like the reading of whoever read ﴿Splitter of the dawn and He made the night for rest﴾ [al-An'am: 96]. Al-Hasan and Humayd ibn Qays read rusulan with the sukun on the sin, and this is the dialect of Tamim. Al-Zamakhshari said: it was also read "alladhi fatara al-samawati wa al-ard wa ja'ala al-malaikata." Whoever reads fatara and ja'ala, these clauses should be a report from the servant of the favors which He has bestowed upon us, as you say: "The favor is to Zayd, who did good to us with such-and-such, gave us such-and-such," so that this serves as a clarification of his beautiful act; likewise in His saying fatara, ja'ala, because in that are countless blessings. Whoever reads wa-jaʿili, then the more apparent view is that both are active participles in the sense of the past, so that they are epithets of Allah; and the disagreement arises concerning the accusative of rusulan. The view of al-Sirafi is that it is accusative by the active participle, and although it is past, since it cannot be made to govern two nouns, the second is put in the accusative. The view of Abu ʿAli is that it is accusative by an implied verb; and the weighing between the two views is mentioned in grammar. As for whoever reads al-malaikata in the accusative, it is derived according to the view of al-Kisai and Hisham on the permissibility of the past tense governing the accusative, and in that case its i'rab is as an apposition. It was also said: it is in the future, its estimate being "He makes the angels messengers," and its i'rab is likewise an apposition. The meaning of rusulan is by revelation and other of His commands; and He does not mean all the angels, for they are not all messengers. Among the messengers are Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and Izra'il, and the angels who follow one another, and the angels who guide, the rulers of justice, and others, like the angel whom Allah sent to the blind man, the leper, and the bald man.

Translation of the passage:

And ﴿wings﴾ is the plural of janāḥ (wing), in the form of the paucal plural (ṣīghat jam‘ al-qillah), while the analogical form of the plural of abundance (jam‘ al-kathrah) for it would be janaḥ on the pattern faʿal. If that is not attested, then (ajniḥah) is used for both the few and the many. The discussion of (mathnā), (thulātha) and (rubāʿa) was already covered at length at the beginning of al-Nisāʾ, but the exegetes have touched on a discussion of them here. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Mathnā, thulātha and ruʿāb are attributes of the wings, and they are not diptote (lam tanṣarif) because of the repetition of ʿadl (deviation from the original form) in them. This is because they have been deviated from the forms of the cardinal numbers into other forms, just as ʿUmar was deviated from ʿĀmir, and Ḥadhām from Ḥādhimah, and from repetition to non-repetition. As for the attributive function, the state of the deviated form and that from which it deviates is not combined. Do you not see that you say bi-niswatin arbaʿ and bi-rijālin thalāthah, and no attention is paid to it?" End of quote. So he made the preventive cause of diptoting the repetition of ʿadl in them. The well-known view is that they are prevented from taking tanwīn because of the attributive quality and ʿadl. As for his saying "Do you not see," he analogized the attributive quality in this deviated form to the attributive quality in (afʿal) and in thalāthah, and this is not correct, because the mere attributive quality is not counted by them as a cause; rather they stipulated a condition for it. The condition is not present in arbaʿ, because its condition is that it does not accept the feminine marker tāʾ. Nor is its condition present in thalāthah, because it is not made a cause together with the feminine. So al-Zamakhsharī's analogy is a faulty analogy, since he overlooked the condition for the attribute to be a cause. Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: "They were deviated from the state of indefiniteness, so they became definite by deviation; therefore they are diptote because of ʿadl and definiteness. It was also said: because of ʿadl and the attributive quality." End of quote. This second view is the well-known one, and the first is the opinion of some of the Kufans. The apparent meaning is that one angel has two wings, another has three, another has four, and another has more than that, based on what is reported: that Jibrīl has six hundred wings, two of which span from east to west. Qatādah said: al-Zamakhsharī began to discuss the manner of these wings and the form of the three, with things that are of no benefit, saying: "Consult that in his book." Another group said: the meaning is that each side of the angel has two wings, and some have three, and some have four; otherwise, if one had three wings, they would not be balanced in what we see of wings in the usual way. It was also said: rather, one may have three wings, as is found in some animals. The apparent meaning of the wings is what the word was set for in the language.

Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Rāzī said: he discusses this in his explanation of the words ﴿Praise be to God, Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, and this is what we related from him: that His saying ﴿Who made the angels messengers having wings, two, three or four﴾ — the least that exists for one with a wing — is an indication of direction. Its explanation: God has nothing above Him, and everything is under His power and blessing. The angels have a face toward God, from which they take His blessings and give to those below them what they have taken, by God's permission, as He said, ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 193] ﴿upon your heart﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 194], and His saying ﴿Taught by one mighty in power﴾ [al-Najm: 5], and He said concerning them ﴿and those who arrange affairs, by command﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 5]; the Nāziʿāt are thus two wings. Among them is one who does what good he does through an intermediary, and among them is one who does it without an intermediary. The one who acts through an intermediary among them has three directions, and among them is one who has four directions and more. End of quote. His discussion in this and in ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾ is a strange discussion, and it is not in accordance with the way the Arabs understand the meanings of the words, which he burdened with what he burdened them with. The apparent meaning is that mathnā and what follows it are attributes of the wings. It was also said that ﴿having wings﴾ is parenthetical, (mathnā) is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), and the governing element is an implied verb indicated by ﴿messengers﴾, i.e., they are sent two by two, three by three, four by four. It was said: He made them possessors of wings only because, when He made them messengers, He gave them wings so that the command would be carried out more quickly and the decree executed more swiftly. For the distance between the heaven and the earth is not covered on foot except in years, so wings were given to them so that they might reach the distant place in a short time, like birds.

﴿He increases in creation what He wills﴾: this confirms what arises in souls of wonder and astonishment at the report of the angels possessing wings; that is, this is no novelty in God's power, for He increases in His creation what He wills. The apparent meaning is the generality of creation. al-Farrāʾ said: this refers to the wings that the angels have, that is, He increases the wings in the creation of the angels. They also said: this increase includes beautiful form, or beautiful voice, or beautiful handwriting, or elegance in the eyes or nose, or lightness of spirit, or beauty, or curly hair, or intellect, or knowledge, or craftsmanship, or chastity among the poor, or sweetness in the mouth; these sayings are given by way of example, not restriction. The verse is absolute and encompasses every increase in creation, and they have explained this increase by desirable things; and "what He wills" is general and does not specify one desirable thing over another. He concluded the verse with ﴿power over everything﴾, which indicates this. Opening and sending are a metaphor for releasing, and ﴿none can send it forth﴾ stands in place of ﴿none can open it﴾; the meaning is: whatever God seeks.

﴿of mercy﴾: that is, of blessing and provision, or rain, or health, or security, or other kinds of His favors that cannot be counted. What is reported from the early exegetes about explaining mercy by a particular thing is not meant as a restriction; it is only an example. al-Zamakhsharī said: the indefiniteness of "mercy" is for generality and vagueness, as if he said: of whatever mercy it may be, heavenly or earthly, no one can hold it back or restrain it, and whatever God withholds, no one can release it. End of quote. The generality is understood from the conditional noun and from "of mercy" serving to clarify that general term as to what kind it is. This is one of the cases where the indefinite singular is used in place of the definite plural which corresponds in generality to the conditional noun; its implied form is: of mercies. "Min" is in the position of a circumstantial clause, i.e., being among mercies, and it cannot be in the position of an attribute because the conditional noun is not qualified. The apparent meaning is that His saying ﴿and whatever He withholds﴾ is general, covering mercy and other things, since no specification was mentioned for it; so it remains general over everything He withholds. If its explanation is ﴿of mercy﴾ and it has been omitted because the first indicates it, then the masculine pronoun in ﴿none can send it forth after Him﴾ is taken according to the wording of "mā," while the feminine in ﴿none can withhold it﴾ is taken according to its meaning, since its meaning is mercy. It was also read: "fa-lā mursila lahā," with the feminine pronoun, and this is evidence that the explanation is ﴿of mercy﴾, which was omitted because the preceding clause indicates it. From Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿of mercy﴾ is of the category of repentance (tawbah), ﴿none can withhold it﴾, i.e., they repent if they wish and if they refuse; ﴿and whatever He withholds﴾ is of the category of ..., ﴿none can send it forth after Him﴾, so they do not repent. Also from him: ﴿of mercy﴾ means of guidance. al-Zamakhsharī said: If you say: what do you say about one who explained mercy as repentance and attributed it to Ibn ʿAbbās? I say: he meant by repentance: guidance toward it and success in it, which is what Ibn ʿAbbās meant; if he said it, it is acceptable; but if he meant that if the sinner wills to repent he repents, and if he does not will, he does not repent, it is rejected, because God wills repentance forever, and it is not permissible for Him not to will it. End of quote, and this is in the way of the Muʿtazilah.

﴿after Him﴾ is by omission of a noun: that is, after His withholding, like His saying ﴿who then can guide him after God?﴾ [al-Jāthiyah: 23], i.e., after God's leading astray of him, because before it is ﴿and God led him astray knowingly﴾, like His saying ﴿whom God leads astray, there is no guide for him﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 186]. al-Zamakhsharī estimated it as "after the guidance of God," which is a faulty estimate that does not suit the verse; he proceeded in it in the way of the Muʿtazilah.

﴿And He is the Mighty﴾: the Overpowering, capable of sending and withholding; ﴿the Wise﴾: who sends and withholds according to what His wisdom requires.

﴿O people﴾: address to the Quraysh, and it is directed to every believer and disbeliever, especially whoever worships other than God; and He reminded them of His blessings in their creation. ﴿Remember﴾ is not a command to remember with the tongue, but with it and with the heart, and by guarding the blessing from ingratitude and by thanking; like your saying to one whom you have favored: "Remember my favors upon you," meaning preserve them and be thankful for them. All are immersed in God's blessing. So the address is general in wording, even though this was revealed because of the Quraysh; then He asked as a question for the purpose of affirmation.

﴿Is there any creator other than God?﴾ That is: there is no god except the Creator; what you worship of idols is not. Ibn Wththāb, Shaqīq, Abū Jaʿfar, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ﴿ghayri﴾ in the genitive, as an adjective agreeing with the wording, and ﴿min khāliq﴾ is the subject. ﴿Provides for you﴾: they permitted it to be the predicate of the subject, or an attribute of it, or a new sentence, and on these two possibilities the predicate is omitted, its estimate being "for you." Shaybah, ʿĪsā, al-Ḥasan and the rest of the seven read ﴿ghayru﴾ in the nominative, and they permitted it to be an adjective agreeing with the position, just as the predicate was an adjective agreeing with the wording; and this is more apparent for the harmony of the two readings; and that it be the predicate of the subject, and that it be the agent of the active participle ﴿khāliq﴾, since it relies on the interrogative particle, so its governing is permitted, like your saying: "Is Zayd standing?" according to one of its aspects. In this there is consideration: that an active participle, or what functions like it, when it relies on an interrogative particle and is made to function like a verb so that it raises what follows it, can one prefix to it "min" of universal quantification, saying "Is there any standing man, the Zaydūn?" as you say "Is standing the Zaydūn?" The apparent view is that it is not permitted. Do you not see that when it functions like a verb, it does not contain generality, contrary to when you prefix "min" to it? I do not know a parallel to it in the speech of the Arabs, and one should not advance the permissibility of such a thing except with a hearing from Arabic speech. Al-Faḍl ibn Ibrāhīm al-Naḥwī read ﴿ghayra﴾ in the accusative as an exception, and the predicate is either ﴿provides for you﴾ or an omitted one, and ﴿provides for you﴾ is a new sentence; and when ﴿provides for you﴾ is a new sentence it is better, because the truth of "creator" applied to other than God is negated, unlike when it is an attribute, for an attribute restricts, so there would be a creator other than God, but he would not be a provider. The meaning of ﴿from the heaven﴾ is with rain, ﴿and the earth﴾ with plants; ﴿there is no god but Him﴾ is an independent sentence with no place in the grammatical structure.

﴿Then how are you turned away?﴾: that is, how are they turned from monotheism to polytheism; and "that they deny you" leads to matters; the discussion of this has already been given.

﴿Indeed the promise of God is true﴾: it encompasses all that He promised of reward, punishment and other things. The majority read ﴿al-gharūr﴾ with a fatḥah on the ghayn, and Ibn ʿAbbās explained it as the Shayṭān. Abū Ḥaywah and Abū al-Sammāl read it with a ḍammah, as the plural of gharr, or as a verbal noun, like His saying ﴿and he made them fall by deception﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 22]. The discussion of this has already been covered at the end of Luqmān.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 35, verses 1–8 (part 3 of 3):

﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you.﴾ His enmity dates back to our father Adam. And what greater enmity is there than that he said about his descendants, ﴿I will surely mislead them all﴾ [Sad: 82], ﴿and I will surely lead them astray﴾ [an-Nisa: 119]? ﴿So take him as an enemy﴾, meaning by boycotting and opposing him, by following the Sharia. Then he explained that his aim in calling his party was only to have them tormented in the Fire, sharing the punishment with them. He is therefore extremely eager for this, so that he may prove the truth of his words, ﴿I will surely mislead them﴾ [al-Hijr: 39], ﴿and I will surely lead them astray﴾ [an-Nisa: 119]. For sharing in what is harmful may bring some consolation, unlike being alone in punishment. Then he mentioned the two groups and what has been prepared for each of them of punishment and reward. He began with the disbelievers because of the proximity to his words, ﴿He only calls his party﴾, so he followed the report about the disbeliever with his state in the Hereafter. Ibn Atiyyah said: The lam in ﴿liyakūna﴾ ("that they may be") is the lam of becoming (lam al-sayrurah), because he did not call them to the blaze; rather, it happened that their affair became, as a result of his calling, to that end. End of quotation. We say: This is of what is expressed by the cause, using what results from it: their being called to disbelief, and the punishment resulting from it. And ﴿those who disbelieved﴾ and ﴿those who believed﴾ are subjects (mubtada'an). Some allowed that ﴿those who disbelieved﴾ could be in the genitive position as a substitute (badal) for ﴿the companions of the blaze﴾, or as a descriptive qualifier (sifah), and in the accusative position as a substitute for ﴿his party﴾, and in the nominative position as a substitute for the pronoun in ﴿liyakūnū﴾. All of this is far from the eloquence of the division and the strength of the structure.

﴿Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him, so that he sees it as good [...]﴾: meaning, so that he sees the evil of his deed as good. Man (من) is a relative subject (mubtada' mawsul), and its predicate is omitted. What the analysis requires is that the implied meaning be: "like one for whom it has not been made attractive," as in His words, ﴿Is one who is upon clear evidence from his Lord like one for whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive?﴾ [Muhammad: 14], ﴿Is one who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind?﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 19], ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life...?﴾ [al-An'am: 122], then He said, ﴿like one whose likeness is in darkness﴾ [al-An'am: 122]. This was said by al-Kisa'i, meaning its implied form is: "his soul goes out after them in regrets," because of the indication of ﴿so do not let your soul go out after them﴾. It was also said that the implied meaning is: "he saw it as good, so Allah misguided him, like one whom Allah guided," so that was omitted because of the indication of ﴿Indeed, Allah misguides whom He wills﴾. Az-Zajjaj mentioned these two views. Az-Zamakhshari explained here ﴿He misguides whom He wills﴾ according to his method in various places of his book, that misguidance is His forsaking him and leaving him to his own affair, and he used many expressions to this meaning. The majority read ﴿Is one whose [evil deed] has been made attractive﴾ in the passive voice, with ﴿evil﴾ in the nominative case (sū'u). ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read: zayyana la-hu sū'a, in the active voice, with sū'a in the accusative. He is also reported to have read asū'a in the form of af'al in the accusative. The worst of his deed is shirk. The reading of Talhah is: a-man without the fa'. The author of al-Lawami said: It is an interrogative with the meaning of the common reading, for affirmation (taqrir). It may also be in the meaning of the vocative particle, so the complete form has been omitted, as the answer has been omitted in the well-known form. End of quotation. By "the answer" he means the predicate of the subject, and by "the complete form" he means what is conveyed by it, meaning: reflect and return to Allah. ﴿Indeed, Allah misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾ is a consolation to the Messenger (ﷺ) regarding the disbelief of his people, and an obligation of submission to Allah in His misguiding whom He wills and guiding whom He wills. The majority read ﴿So do not let your soul go [after them]﴾ in the active voice from dhahaba, with nafsuka as the subject. Abu Ja'far, Qatadah, ʿIsa, al-Ashhab, Shaybah, Abu Haywah, Humayd, al-A'mash, and Ibn Muhaysin read tudhhib from adhhaba, with the pronoun of the addressee ﴿your soul﴾ as the object in the accusative. It is narrated from Nafi'. Al-hasrah is the grief of the soul over the loss of a matter. ﴿Regrets﴾ (hasarat) is in the accusative as a object of purpose (maf'ul min ajlihi), meaning: "do not let your soul perish out of regrets." ʿAlayhim is related to ﴿tadhhab﴾, as you say: "he perished for him out of love," and "he died for him out of sorrow." Or it is an explanation of the one regretted over, and it is not related to ḥasarāt because it is a verbal noun, and its complement cannot precede it. Az-Zamakhshari said: It may also be a circumstantial state (hal), as if all of it became regrets due to the intensity of grief, as Jarir said:

*Ceaseless heat has worn their flesh away along with the night-journey, until they departed as breasts and chests.*

He means: they returned as breasts and chests, that is, nothing remained except their breasts and chests. From the same is His saying:

*Upon their trail my soul falls away in regrets, and their remembrance for me is sickness.*

End of quotation. What was mentioned, that "breasts and chests" are circumstantial states, is the view of Sibawayh. Al-Mubarrad said: It is a specification (tamyiz) transferred from the subject, meaning: until their breasts and chests departed. Then He threatened them with punishment for their evil conduct, saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾, meaning: He will therefore recompense them for it.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 35, verses 1–8 (part 1 of 3):

Surat Fatir is Meccan, and it has forty-five verses.
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿All praise is due to Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, who made the angels messengers having wings, two or three or four. He adds to creation what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾ ﴿Whatever mercy Allah grants to people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release after Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ ﴿O mankind, remember the favor of Allah upon you. Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? There is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded?﴾ ﴿And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then already were messengers denied before you. And to Allah are returned all matters.﴾ ﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is true, so let not the worldly life delude you, and let not the Deceiver delude you concerning Allah.﴾ ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party that they may be among the companions of the Blaze.﴾ ﴿Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment, but those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ ﴿Then is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him so that he sees it as good [equal to one guided]? For indeed, Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So do not let yourself go in grief over them. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.﴾ ﴿And it is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, and We drive them to a dead land and revive thereby the earth after its death. Thus will be the resurrection.﴾ [Fatir: 9] ﴿Whoever desires honor — to Allah belongs all honor. To Him ascends good speech, and righteous deeds raise it. But those who plot evil deeds will have a severe punishment, and the plotting of those — it will perish.﴾ [Fatir: 10] ﴿And Allah created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then made you into pairs. No female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge. And no one is granted a lengthened life or has his life shortened except that it is in a Record. Indeed, that is easy for Allah.﴾ [Fatir: 11] ﴿And not alike are the two bodies of water: one is sweet, fresh, pleasant to drink, and the other is salty and bitter. And from both you eat fresh meat and extract ornaments you wear, and you see the ships plowing through them that you may seek of His bounty; and perhaps you will be grateful.﴾ [Fatir: 12] ﴿He merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running to a specified term. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. And those you invoke other than Him do not possess [so much as] a date-pit membrane.﴾ [Fatir: 13] ﴿If you invoke them, they do not hear your call; and if they heard, they would not respond to you. And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your associating them with Him. And none can inform you like an [All-]Acquainted.﴾ [Fatir: 14] ﴿O mankind, you are the poor toward Allah, and Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.﴾ [Fatir: 15] ﴿If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation.﴾ [Fatir: 16] ﴿And that is not difficult for Allah.﴾ [Fatir: 17] ﴿No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a relative. You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen and establish prayer. And whoever purifies himself does so only for his own soul. And to Allah is the destination.﴾ [Fatir: 18] ﴿And not alike are the blind and the seeing,﴾ [Fatir: 19] ﴿nor are darknesses and light,﴾ [Fatir: 20] ﴿nor shade and heat,﴾ [Fatir: 21] ﴿nor are the living and the dead alike. Indeed, Allah causes to hear whom He wills, but you cannot make hear those who are in the graves.﴾ [Fatir: 22] ﴿You are not but a warner.﴾ [Fatir: 23] ﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them.﴾ [Fatir: 24] ﴿And if they deny you, those before them had already denied; their messengers came to them with clear proofs and with scriptures and with the illuminating Book.﴾ [Fatir: 25] ﴿Then I seized those who disbelieved, so how was My denunciation!﴾ [Fatir: 26] ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down rain from the sky, and We bring forth thereby fruits of varying colors? And among the mountains are white and red streaks of varying shades, and [others] extremely black.﴾ [Fatir: 27] ﴿And among people and moving creatures and livestock are those of various colors. Thus, among His servants, only the knowledgeable fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might, Forgiving.﴾ [Fatir: 28] ﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah, establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, hope for a commerce that will never perish,﴾ [Fatir: 29] ﴿that He may give them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty. Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾ [Fatir: 30] ﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth, confirming what was before it. Indeed, Allah is, concerning His servants, All-Knowing and Seeing.﴾ [Fatir: 31] ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants; then among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah. That is the great bounty.﴾ [Fatir: 32] ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence they will enter, adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their clothing therein is silk.﴾ [Fatir: 33] ﴿And they will say, "All praise is due to Allah, who has removed from us grief. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative,﴾ [Fatir: 34] ﴿who has settled us in the home of settlement from His bounty; there touches us not fatigue, nor touches us therein weariness."﴾ [Fatir: 35]

Al-Qitmir: it is well known that it is the thin skin that is on the date-pit, and the statements of the exegetes will come. Al-judad: plural of judda, which is a path formed in the land or the mountain, like a great piece continuous in length. Al-Zamakhshari said: al-judad are the streaks and the paths. Labid said: "or a course (judad) of the single one." It is said: judda of the donkey for the black mark on its back, and a gazelle may have two musk-scented streaks separating the colors of its back and its belly. End. The poet said:

"As if the streaks and the judda of its back were beads among which glitters a gleam."

The judda: the line that is in the middle of its back, describing a wild donkey. Al-gharibib: the intensely black. Laghiba yalghabu lughuban: he became weary.

* *

This surah is Meccan. When Allah, exalted, mentioned at the end of the preceding surah the destruction of the disbelievers, enemies of the believers, and placed them in the abodes of punishment, it became incumbent upon the believers to praise Him, to thank Him for His blessings, and to describe Him with His great favors, as in His saying: ﴿So the last of the people who did wrong were cut off. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-An'am: 45].

Al-Dahhak and al-Zuhri read fatara, making it a past-tense verb and putting in the accusative what follows it. Abu al-Fadl al-Razi said: either by supposing an implied alladhi, so that it is an epithet for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; or by estimating qad before it, so that it has the sense of a circumstantial clause. End. Omitting the relative noun is not permitted according to the Basrans. As for the circumstantial clause, it would be a narrated circumstance; but the better view, in my opinion, is that it is the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e., He is the One who originated (fatara). The explanation of ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾ has already been given, and that the meaning is "creator of them after they were not." The heavens and the earth are an expression for the world.

Abu Abdullah al-Razi said: praise is generally for a blessing, and Allah's blessings are immediate. ﴿Praise be to Allah who created the heavens and the earth and made darknesses and light﴾ [al-An'am: 1] points to the immediate blessing, and its evidence is ﴿He is the One who created you from clay, then decreed a term﴾ [al-An'am: 2]. And ﴿Praise be to Allah who revealed to His servant the Book﴾ [al-Kahf: 1] also points to it; and it is piety, for piety and righteousness come through the Law and the Book. Praise in Surat Saba' points to the blessing of bringing into being and of gathering, and its evidence is ﴿He knows what enters the earth and what emerges from it﴾ [Saba': 2], and His saying ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us"﴾ [Saba': 3]. And here it points to the blessing of endurance in the Hereafter, and its evidence is ﴿and the angels will receive them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 103]. (So Fatir of the heavens and the earth is the one who splits them, for the descent of spirits from the sky and the emergence of bodies from the earth; its evidence is ﴿Who made the angels messengers having wings﴾, that is, on that day.) Thus the beginning of this surah is connected to the end of what came before; because "as was done with their likes before" is a clarification of the cutting off of the hope of one who was in disquieting doubt. When He mentioned their state, He mentioned the state of the believer and gave him good news of the sending of the angels to them as bringers of good tidings, and that He opens for them the doors of mercy.

al-Hasan read jaʿiluh with nominative (jāʿilun), i.e., He is the maker; ʿAbd al-Warith from Abu ʿAmr read jaʿilu with nominative without tanwin, and al-malāʾikata in the accusative, the tanwin being dropped because of the meeting of two unvocalized letters. Ibn Yaʿmar and Khulayd ibn Nashit read jaʿala as a past-tense verb, with al-malāʾikata in the accusative, after reading fāṭiri with an alif and the genitive, like the reading of whoever read ﴿Splitter of the dawn and He made the night for rest﴾ [al-An'am: 96]. Al-Hasan and Humayd ibn Qays read rusulan with the sukun on the sin, and this is the dialect of Tamim. Al-Zamakhshari said: it was also read "alladhi fatara al-samawati wa al-ard wa ja'ala al-malaikata." Whoever reads fatara and ja'ala, these clauses should be a report from the servant of the favors which He has bestowed upon us, as you say: "The favor is to Zayd, who did good to us with such-and-such, gave us such-and-such," so that this serves as a clarification of his beautiful act; likewise in His saying fatara, ja'ala, because in that are countless blessings. Whoever reads wa-jaʿili, then the more apparent view is that both are active participles in the sense of the past, so that they are epithets of Allah; and the disagreement arises concerning the accusative of rusulan. The view of al-Sirafi is that it is accusative by the active participle, and although it is past, since it cannot be made to govern two nouns, the second is put in the accusative. The view of Abu ʿAli is that it is accusative by an implied verb; and the weighing between the two views is mentioned in grammar. As for whoever reads al-malaikata in the accusative, it is derived according to the view of al-Kisai and Hisham on the permissibility of the past tense governing the accusative, and in that case its i'rab is as an apposition. It was also said: it is in the future, its estimate being "He makes the angels messengers," and its i'rab is likewise an apposition. The meaning of rusulan is by revelation and other of His commands; and He does not mean all the angels, for they are not all messengers. Among the messengers are Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and Izra'il, and the angels who follow one another, and the angels who guide, the rulers of justice, and others, like the angel whom Allah sent to the blind man, the leper, and the bald man.

Translation of the passage:

And ﴿wings﴾ is the plural of janāḥ (wing), in the form of the paucal plural (ṣīghat jam‘ al-qillah), while the analogical form of the plural of abundance (jam‘ al-kathrah) for it would be janaḥ on the pattern faʿal. If that is not attested, then (ajniḥah) is used for both the few and the many. The discussion of (mathnā), (thulātha) and (rubāʿa) was already covered at length at the beginning of al-Nisāʾ, but the exegetes have touched on a discussion of them here. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Mathnā, thulātha and ruʿāb are attributes of the wings, and they are not diptote (lam tanṣarif) because of the repetition of ʿadl (deviation from the original form) in them. This is because they have been deviated from the forms of the cardinal numbers into other forms, just as ʿUmar was deviated from ʿĀmir, and Ḥadhām from Ḥādhimah, and from repetition to non-repetition. As for the attributive function, the state of the deviated form and that from which it deviates is not combined. Do you not see that you say bi-niswatin arbaʿ and bi-rijālin thalāthah, and no attention is paid to it?" End of quote. So he made the preventive cause of diptoting the repetition of ʿadl in them. The well-known view is that they are prevented from taking tanwīn because of the attributive quality and ʿadl. As for his saying "Do you not see," he analogized the attributive quality in this deviated form to the attributive quality in (afʿal) and in thalāthah, and this is not correct, because the mere attributive quality is not counted by them as a cause; rather they stipulated a condition for it. The condition is not present in arbaʿ, because its condition is that it does not accept the feminine marker tāʾ. Nor is its condition present in thalāthah, because it is not made a cause together with the feminine. So al-Zamakhsharī's analogy is a faulty analogy, since he overlooked the condition for the attribute to be a cause. Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: "They were deviated from the state of indefiniteness, so they became definite by deviation; therefore they are diptote because of ʿadl and definiteness. It was also said: because of ʿadl and the attributive quality." End of quote. This second view is the well-known one, and the first is the opinion of some of the Kufans. The apparent meaning is that one angel has two wings, another has three, another has four, and another has more than that, based on what is reported: that Jibrīl has six hundred wings, two of which span from east to west. Qatādah said: al-Zamakhsharī began to discuss the manner of these wings and the form of the three, with things that are of no benefit, saying: "Consult that in his book." Another group said: the meaning is that each side of the angel has two wings, and some have three, and some have four; otherwise, if one had three wings, they would not be balanced in what we see of wings in the usual way. It was also said: rather, one may have three wings, as is found in some animals. The apparent meaning of the wings is what the word was set for in the language.

Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Rāzī said: he discusses this in his explanation of the words ﴿Praise be to God, Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, and this is what we related from him: that His saying ﴿Who made the angels messengers having wings, two, three or four﴾ — the least that exists for one with a wing — is an indication of direction. Its explanation: God has nothing above Him, and everything is under His power and blessing. The angels have a face toward God, from which they take His blessings and give to those below them what they have taken, by God's permission, as He said, ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 193] ﴿upon your heart﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 194], and His saying ﴿Taught by one mighty in power﴾ [al-Najm: 5], and He said concerning them ﴿and those who arrange affairs, by command﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 5]; the Nāziʿāt are thus two wings. Among them is one who does what good he does through an intermediary, and among them is one who does it without an intermediary. The one who acts through an intermediary among them has three directions, and among them is one who has four directions and more. End of quote. His discussion in this and in ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾ is a strange discussion, and it is not in accordance with the way the Arabs understand the meanings of the words, which he burdened with what he burdened them with. The apparent meaning is that mathnā and what follows it are attributes of the wings. It was also said that ﴿having wings﴾ is parenthetical, (mathnā) is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), and the governing element is an implied verb indicated by ﴿messengers﴾, i.e., they are sent two by two, three by three, four by four. It was said: He made them possessors of wings only because, when He made them messengers, He gave them wings so that the command would be carried out more quickly and the decree executed more swiftly. For the distance between the heaven and the earth is not covered on foot except in years, so wings were given to them so that they might reach the distant place in a short time, like birds.

﴿He increases in creation what He wills﴾: this confirms what arises in souls of wonder and astonishment at the report of the angels possessing wings; that is, this is no novelty in God's power, for He increases in His creation what He wills. The apparent meaning is the generality of creation. al-Farrāʾ said: this refers to the wings that the angels have, that is, He increases the wings in the creation of the angels. They also said: this increase includes beautiful form, or beautiful voice, or beautiful handwriting, or elegance in the eyes or nose, or lightness of spirit, or beauty, or curly hair, or intellect, or knowledge, or craftsmanship, or chastity among the poor, or sweetness in the mouth; these sayings are given by way of example, not restriction. The verse is absolute and encompasses every increase in creation, and they have explained this increase by desirable things; and "what He wills" is general and does not specify one desirable thing over another. He concluded the verse with ﴿power over everything﴾, which indicates this. Opening and sending are a metaphor for releasing, and ﴿none can send it forth﴾ stands in place of ﴿none can open it﴾; the meaning is: whatever God seeks.

﴿of mercy﴾: that is, of blessing and provision, or rain, or health, or security, or other kinds of His favors that cannot be counted. What is reported from the early exegetes about explaining mercy by a particular thing is not meant as a restriction; it is only an example. al-Zamakhsharī said: the indefiniteness of "mercy" is for generality and vagueness, as if he said: of whatever mercy it may be, heavenly or earthly, no one can hold it back or restrain it, and whatever God withholds, no one can release it. End of quote. The generality is understood from the conditional noun and from "of mercy" serving to clarify that general term as to what kind it is. This is one of the cases where the indefinite singular is used in place of the definite plural which corresponds in generality to the conditional noun; its implied form is: of mercies. "Min" is in the position of a circumstantial clause, i.e., being among mercies, and it cannot be in the position of an attribute because the conditional noun is not qualified. The apparent meaning is that His saying ﴿and whatever He withholds﴾ is general, covering mercy and other things, since no specification was mentioned for it; so it remains general over everything He withholds. If its explanation is ﴿of mercy﴾ and it has been omitted because the first indicates it, then the masculine pronoun in ﴿none can send it forth after Him﴾ is taken according to the wording of "mā," while the feminine in ﴿none can withhold it﴾ is taken according to its meaning, since its meaning is mercy. It was also read: "fa-lā mursila lahā," with the feminine pronoun, and this is evidence that the explanation is ﴿of mercy﴾, which was omitted because the preceding clause indicates it. From Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿of mercy﴾ is of the category of repentance (tawbah), ﴿none can withhold it﴾, i.e., they repent if they wish and if they refuse; ﴿and whatever He withholds﴾ is of the category of ..., ﴿none can send it forth after Him﴾, so they do not repent. Also from him: ﴿of mercy﴾ means of guidance. al-Zamakhsharī said: If you say: what do you say about one who explained mercy as repentance and attributed it to Ibn ʿAbbās? I say: he meant by repentance: guidance toward it and success in it, which is what Ibn ʿAbbās meant; if he said it, it is acceptable; but if he meant that if the sinner wills to repent he repents, and if he does not will, he does not repent, it is rejected, because God wills repentance forever, and it is not permissible for Him not to will it. End of quote, and this is in the way of the Muʿtazilah.

﴿after Him﴾ is by omission of a noun: that is, after His withholding, like His saying ﴿who then can guide him after God?﴾ [al-Jāthiyah: 23], i.e., after God's leading astray of him, because before it is ﴿and God led him astray knowingly﴾, like His saying ﴿whom God leads astray, there is no guide for him﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 186]. al-Zamakhsharī estimated it as "after the guidance of God," which is a faulty estimate that does not suit the verse; he proceeded in it in the way of the Muʿtazilah.

﴿And He is the Mighty﴾: the Overpowering, capable of sending and withholding; ﴿the Wise﴾: who sends and withholds according to what His wisdom requires.

﴿O people﴾: address to the Quraysh, and it is directed to every believer and disbeliever, especially whoever worships other than God; and He reminded them of His blessings in their creation. ﴿Remember﴾ is not a command to remember with the tongue, but with it and with the heart, and by guarding the blessing from ingratitude and by thanking; like your saying to one whom you have favored: "Remember my favors upon you," meaning preserve them and be thankful for them. All are immersed in God's blessing. So the address is general in wording, even though this was revealed because of the Quraysh; then He asked as a question for the purpose of affirmation.

﴿Is there any creator other than God?﴾ That is: there is no god except the Creator; what you worship of idols is not. Ibn Wththāb, Shaqīq, Abū Jaʿfar, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read ﴿ghayri﴾ in the genitive, as an adjective agreeing with the wording, and ﴿min khāliq﴾ is the subject. ﴿Provides for you﴾: they permitted it to be the predicate of the subject, or an attribute of it, or a new sentence, and on these two possibilities the predicate is omitted, its estimate being "for you." Shaybah, ʿĪsā, al-Ḥasan and the rest of the seven read ﴿ghayru﴾ in the nominative, and they permitted it to be an adjective agreeing with the position, just as the predicate was an adjective agreeing with the wording; and this is more apparent for the harmony of the two readings; and that it be the predicate of the subject, and that it be the agent of the active participle ﴿khāliq﴾, since it relies on the interrogative particle, so its governing is permitted, like your saying: "Is Zayd standing?" according to one of its aspects. In this there is consideration: that an active participle, or what functions like it, when it relies on an interrogative particle and is made to function like a verb so that it raises what follows it, can one prefix to it "min" of universal quantification, saying "Is there any standing man, the Zaydūn?" as you say "Is standing the Zaydūn?" The apparent view is that it is not permitted. Do you not see that when it functions like a verb, it does not contain generality, contrary to when you prefix "min" to it? I do not know a parallel to it in the speech of the Arabs, and one should not advance the permissibility of such a thing except with a hearing from Arabic speech. Al-Faḍl ibn Ibrāhīm al-Naḥwī read ﴿ghayra﴾ in the accusative as an exception, and the predicate is either ﴿provides for you﴾ or an omitted one, and ﴿provides for you﴾ is a new sentence; and when ﴿provides for you﴾ is a new sentence it is better, because the truth of "creator" applied to other than God is negated, unlike when it is an attribute, for an attribute restricts, so there would be a creator other than God, but he would not be a provider. The meaning of ﴿from the heaven﴾ is with rain, ﴿and the earth﴾ with plants; ﴿there is no god but Him﴾ is an independent sentence with no place in the grammatical structure.

﴿Then how are you turned away?﴾: that is, how are they turned from monotheism to polytheism; and "that they deny you" leads to matters; the discussion of this has already been given.

﴿Indeed the promise of God is true﴾: it encompasses all that He promised of reward, punishment and other things. The majority read ﴿al-gharūr﴾ with a fatḥah on the ghayn, and Ibn ʿAbbās explained it as the Shayṭān. Abū Ḥaywah and Abū al-Sammāl read it with a ḍammah, as the plural of gharr, or as a verbal noun, like His saying ﴿and he made them fall by deception﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 22]. The discussion of this has already been covered at the end of Luqmān.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 35, verses 1–8 (part 3 of 3):

﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you.﴾ His enmity dates back to our father Adam. And what greater enmity is there than that he said about his descendants, ﴿I will surely mislead them all﴾ [Sad: 82], ﴿and I will surely lead them astray﴾ [an-Nisa: 119]? ﴿So take him as an enemy﴾, meaning by boycotting and opposing him, by following the Sharia. Then he explained that his aim in calling his party was only to have them tormented in the Fire, sharing the punishment with them. He is therefore extremely eager for this, so that he may prove the truth of his words, ﴿I will surely mislead them﴾ [al-Hijr: 39], ﴿and I will surely lead them astray﴾ [an-Nisa: 119]. For sharing in what is harmful may bring some consolation, unlike being alone in punishment. Then he mentioned the two groups and what has been prepared for each of them of punishment and reward. He began with the disbelievers because of the proximity to his words, ﴿He only calls his party﴾, so he followed the report about the disbeliever with his state in the Hereafter. Ibn Atiyyah said: The lam in ﴿liyakūna﴾ ("that they may be") is the lam of becoming (lam al-sayrurah), because he did not call them to the blaze; rather, it happened that their affair became, as a result of his calling, to that end. End of quotation. We say: This is of what is expressed by the cause, using what results from it: their being called to disbelief, and the punishment resulting from it. And ﴿those who disbelieved﴾ and ﴿those who believed﴾ are subjects (mubtada'an). Some allowed that ﴿those who disbelieved﴾ could be in the genitive position as a substitute (badal) for ﴿the companions of the blaze﴾, or as a descriptive qualifier (sifah), and in the accusative position as a substitute for ﴿his party﴾, and in the nominative position as a substitute for the pronoun in ﴿liyakūnū﴾. All of this is far from the eloquence of the division and the strength of the structure.

﴿Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him, so that he sees it as good [...]﴾: meaning, so that he sees the evil of his deed as good. Man (من) is a relative subject (mubtada' mawsul), and its predicate is omitted. What the analysis requires is that the implied meaning be: "like one for whom it has not been made attractive," as in His words, ﴿Is one who is upon clear evidence from his Lord like one for whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive?﴾ [Muhammad: 14], ﴿Is one who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind?﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 19], ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life...?﴾ [al-An'am: 122], then He said, ﴿like one whose likeness is in darkness﴾ [al-An'am: 122]. This was said by al-Kisa'i, meaning its implied form is: "his soul goes out after them in regrets," because of the indication of ﴿so do not let your soul go out after them﴾. It was also said that the implied meaning is: "he saw it as good, so Allah misguided him, like one whom Allah guided," so that was omitted because of the indication of ﴿Indeed, Allah misguides whom He wills﴾. Az-Zajjaj mentioned these two views. Az-Zamakhshari explained here ﴿He misguides whom He wills﴾ according to his method in various places of his book, that misguidance is His forsaking him and leaving him to his own affair, and he used many expressions to this meaning. The majority read ﴿Is one whose [evil deed] has been made attractive﴾ in the passive voice, with ﴿evil﴾ in the nominative case (sū'u). ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read: zayyana la-hu sū'a, in the active voice, with sū'a in the accusative. He is also reported to have read asū'a in the form of af'al in the accusative. The worst of his deed is shirk. The reading of Talhah is: a-man without the fa'. The author of al-Lawami said: It is an interrogative with the meaning of the common reading, for affirmation (taqrir). It may also be in the meaning of the vocative particle, so the complete form has been omitted, as the answer has been omitted in the well-known form. End of quotation. By "the answer" he means the predicate of the subject, and by "the complete form" he means what is conveyed by it, meaning: reflect and return to Allah. ﴿Indeed, Allah misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾ is a consolation to the Messenger (ﷺ) regarding the disbelief of his people, and an obligation of submission to Allah in His misguiding whom He wills and guiding whom He wills. The majority read ﴿So do not let your soul go [after them]﴾ in the active voice from dhahaba, with nafsuka as the subject. Abu Ja'far, Qatadah, ʿIsa, al-Ashhab, Shaybah, Abu Haywah, Humayd, al-A'mash, and Ibn Muhaysin read tudhhib from adhhaba, with the pronoun of the addressee ﴿your soul﴾ as the object in the accusative. It is narrated from Nafi'. Al-hasrah is the grief of the soul over the loss of a matter. ﴿Regrets﴾ (hasarat) is in the accusative as a object of purpose (maf'ul min ajlihi), meaning: "do not let your soul perish out of regrets." ʿAlayhim is related to ﴿tadhhab﴾, as you say: "he perished for him out of love," and "he died for him out of sorrow." Or it is an explanation of the one regretted over, and it is not related to ḥasarāt because it is a verbal noun, and its complement cannot precede it. Az-Zamakhshari said: It may also be a circumstantial state (hal), as if all of it became regrets due to the intensity of grief, as Jarir said:

*Ceaseless heat has worn their flesh away along with the night-journey, until they departed as breasts and chests.*

He means: they returned as breasts and chests, that is, nothing remained except their breasts and chests. From the same is His saying:

*Upon their trail my soul falls away in regrets, and their remembrance for me is sickness.*

End of quotation. What was mentioned, that "breasts and chests" are circumstantial states, is the view of Sibawayh. Al-Mubarrad said: It is a specification (tamyiz) transferred from the subject, meaning: until their breasts and chests departed. Then He threatened them with punishment for their evil conduct, saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾, meaning: He will therefore recompense them for it.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 35, verses 1–8 (part 1 of 3):

Surat Fatir is Meccan, and it has forty-five verses.
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿All praise is due to Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, who made the angels messengers having wings, two or three or four. He adds to creation what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾ ﴿Whatever mercy Allah grants to people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release after Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ ﴿O mankind, remember the favor of Allah upon you. Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? There is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded?﴾ ﴿And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then already were messengers denied before you. And to Allah are returned all matters.﴾ ﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is true, so let not the worldly life delude you, and let not the Deceiver delude you concerning Allah.﴾ ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party that they may be among the companions of the Blaze.﴾ ﴿Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment, but those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ ﴿Then is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him so that he sees it as good [equal to one guided]? For indeed, Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So do not let yourself go in grief over them. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.﴾ ﴿And it is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, and We drive them to a dead land and revive thereby the earth after its death. Thus will be the resurrection.﴾ [Fatir: 9] ﴿Whoever desires honor — to Allah belongs all honor. To Him ascends good speech, and righteous deeds raise it. But those who plot evil deeds will have a severe punishment, and the plotting of those — it will perish.﴾ [Fatir: 10] ﴿And Allah created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then made you into pairs. No female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge. And no one is granted a lengthened life or has his life shortened except that it is in a Record. Indeed, that is easy for Allah.﴾ [Fatir: 11] ﴿And not alike are the two bodies of water: one is sweet, fresh, pleasant to drink, and the other is salty and bitter.
